title: Rabbi Chiyya bar Lulayni (Lulayva, Lulayta)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Taanit 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.25a.19-20) it is told that Rabbi Chiya bar Lulayni heard those clouds saying, "Let us go and pour water in Ammon and Moab." He said before Him, "Master of the Universe, when You gave the Torah to Your people Israel, You went around to all the nations of the world and they did not accept it, and now You give them rain? Throw it here!" They poured it where he was. And there he expounded: "If 'palm' was stated, why was 'cedar' stated?" etc. In the Yerushalmi, [Avodah Zarah beginning of ch. 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.2.1.3), he said in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya; and in [Ketubot ch. 13 halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.13.2.3) and [Nedarim ch. 4 halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.4.2.3), Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Bun and Rabbi Chiya bar Lulayno both say in the name of Shmuel; and in [Nazir ch. 4, end of halakhah 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nazir.4.4.9), they both say in the name of (Rabbi) Shmi; and in [Orlah beginning of ch. 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Orlah.2.1.4), Rabbi Chiya bar Lulayva said to Rabbi Chananya.

We also find that he had students, as in Challah end of ch. 2, [Yoma ch. 2 beginning of halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yoma.2.2.3), [Nedarim beginning of ch. 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.3.1.3), [Nazir ch. 5 halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nazir.5.3.2), [Shevuot ch. 8 halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shevuot.8.3.5): "the students of Rabbi Chiya bar Lulayta," etc.

notes.text: Lulayni, Lulayno, Lulayva and Lulayta are retained as the notice’s variant forms.

The palm-and-cedar homily begins at the end of 25a and [continues on 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.25b.1). The linked Yerushalmi passages preserve the named sources Hoshaya, Shmuel and Shmi, and distinguish the students’ reports from Rabbi Chiya’s own. The digital Orlah has Lulayani where Hyman gives Lulayva. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1267&lang=en) cites several of the same episodes. The exact Challah occurrence remains unconfirmed.
